This appeal is filed by the appellant/accused under Section 374 (2) of Cr.P.C for setting aside the judgment and conviction order passed by the V Additional District and Sessions Judge, Mysuru in S.C.No.174/2010 dated 20.1.2012 for having found guilty and convicted and sentenced the appellant to undergo simple imprisonment for 2 years and pay fine of Rs.5000/- and in default of payment of fine, to undergo simple imprisonment for 3 months for the offence punishable under Section 498(A)
of IPC.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Mysuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and learned HCGP for respondents.
3.

The case of the prosecution is that on the complaint of PW1/Shambhayya the brother of the deceased lodged complaint to the police on 27.05.2010 alleging that her sister, Rani was married to the accused and the marriage was held on 21.5.2004 in the house of the accused at Hosavaaranchi,
village, Hunsur Taluk.

At the time of negotiation of the marriage, the accused said to have demanded Rs.1 lakh cash NC: 2023:KHC:20502 and golden ornaments of 70 gms and it was decided to given Rs.40,000/- cash and 50 gms gold.

Accordingly, the marriage was held and subsequently the accused started ill treating her by demanding Rs.20,000/- as additional dowry and also demanded Rs.20,000/- for the purchase of fertilizer to his tobacco crop.
Due to the non toleration of the harassment, she has committed suicide on 26.5.2010 in the tobacco barren land situated in Sy.No.142 and 143 belonging to the accused.
FIR was lodged and the police arrested the appellant and he was remanded to judicial custody.
Subsequently, he was released on bail, the charge sheet came to be filed, then the case was committed to the court of Sessions.
The accused faced the trial for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304B of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act (DP Act).

4. The prosecution in order to prove its case examined 22 witnesses and got marked 22 documents and 9 material objects and after closing the evidence of the prosecution the statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C was recorded.
The accused case is one of the total denial and he has examined himself as DW2 and also examined one more witnesses as DW1 NC: 2023:KHC:20502 and got marked 12 documents.

After hearing the arguments, the trial court acquitted the accused/appellant for the offence punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of DP Act and Section 304B of IPC but found the appellant guilty and convicted for the offence punishable under Section 498A imposing sentence of 2 years and fine of Rs.5000/- vide judgment dated 20.01.2020.

Being aggrieved by the same, the Nagendra vs State Of Karnataka on 14 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189226210/
2 appellant is before this court.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant has contended the trial court committed error in convicting the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 498A when there is no demand or acceptance of dowry and further demand of dowry in order to prove the case for the offence punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of DP Act, where the trial court acquitted the appellant and also acquitted the appellant under Section 304 B of IPC but convicting for 498A, is not correct.

Though the trial court accepted the evidence of other witnesses and disbelieved the evidence of PW1 for the purpose of demand of dowry and payment of dowry, but harassment under Section 498(A) of IPC is also not proved by the prosecution.
Therefore, convicting the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 498(A) is not correct.
Hence, prayed for allowing the NC: 2023:KHC:20502 appeal.
Alternatively the learned counsel also argued that the appellant was in custody from the date of his arrest on 28.5.2010 and he was on bail.
Subsequently, he was in judicial custody for one year and eight months during the trial.
Therefore, in case the court found appellant guilty for the offence punishable under Section 498(A) then the same shall be given set off as already he has undergone one year eight months in jail.
Hence prayed for allowing the appeal.

6. Per contra, learned HCGP supported the case of the prosecution and judgment of the trial court and contended that as per the evidence of PW1, the brother and evidence of some of the villagers,
where they have stated the demand of dowry prior to the marriage and subsequently the accused demanded Rs.20,000/- for buying the fertilizer due to which she has committed suicide in the land of the accused.
Though some of the witnesses turned hostile but the complainant and sister Kumari have supported the prosecution case, hence prayed for rejecting the appeal.

7. Having heard the arguments, perused the records, the points that arise for my consideration are:
NC: 2023:KHC:20502 (1) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that after the marriage the accused has harassed the deceased Rani physically and mentally and ill treated her for brining money and demanding additional dowry of Rs.20,000/- thereby he has committed offence punishable under Section 498(A)
of IPC?
(2) Whether the judgment of trial court calls for any interference?
8. Having heard the arguments and perusal of record and prior to the appreciation of evidence, it is worth to mention the evidence adduced by the prosecution.
9. PW1/Shambhayya brother of the deceased and complainant before the police at Ex.P1 who has deposed that the accused came for proposal of marrying his sister.
During the negotiation of marriage he has demanded cash as well as gold and it was decided to give Rs.40,000/- cash instead of Rs.70,000/- and 50 gms gold instead of 70 gms.
The marriage was held in the house of the accused and thereafter there was two children born out of the wedlock.

The accused is having a tobacco garden and he was demanding additional dowry of Rs.20,000/- for purchase of fertilizer,
for which he has given Rs.1000/- about two years prior to the incident.

Thereafter, NC:
Nagendra vs State Of Karnataka on 14 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189226210/
3 2023:KHC:20502
the accused said to have harassed her physically and mentally and demanded money for purchase of fertilizers.

A lengthy cross examination is made by the counsel for accused where this witness had admitted that the amount of Rs.7000/- was paid 3 years prior to the incident and also admitted the marriage was held in the house of the accused and marriage expenditures were borne by the accused.

10. PW2/Ashok son of Lakshmane Gowda and PW3/Boganna were the inquest panch witnesses,
both of them turned hostile in respect of Ex.P10.
However, the death occurred in the house of the accused in the tobacco garden and the suicide is not in dispute.

11. PW4/Kumar who is said to have attended the marriage negotiation, though he has stated there was demand of Rs.70,000/- and agreed to pay Rs.40,000/- by the complainant, he has not stated whether it was paid or not and he was not aware about the same.
12. PW5/E.Raju, Mahazar witness at Ex.P3 for seizing the rope which was plastic rope which was used by the deceased NC: 2023:KHC:20502 for commission of suicide.
Though this witness turned hostile but the factum of commission of suicide is not denied.
13. PW6/Sharanappa who is the brother-in-law of the deceased and husband of the Sister of the deceased.

PW7/Kumari sister of the deceased, both of them have stated about the negotiation and demand of dowry by the accused but both of them turned hostile in respect of harassment and demand and receipt of dowry.
PW6 and PW7, these two witnesses turned hostile and not supported the case of the prosecution case.
So far as marriage and staying of the deceased with the accused is not in dispute.
They also speak about the commission of suicide by the deceased.
14. PW8/Mahadevaiah who is also a villager who attended the marriage negotiation but he has also turned hostile.
Dr.M.R.Udayakumar who conducted the autopsy on the dead body and has issued the post mortem report, according to his evidence there is no external injury and death was due to hanging.
Death by suicidal hanging is not in dispute.
PW10/Chaluvaiha inquest panch witness who has also turned hostile.
17. PW11/Annegowda who is also participated in marriage negotiation and attended the marriage has also turned hostile 18.

PW12/Govinde Gowda who is head of the Village, had attended the marriage negotiation stated there was demand of Rs.70,000/- and 70 gms gold and they decided to give Rs.40,000/- cash and 50 gms gold but he has stated he is not aware whether it is paid or not?

4
19. PW13 /Chandrasekar who is Village Accountant who received the documents at Ex.Nos.P15 and 19 in respect of land in Sy No. 142, the said fact also is not in dispute 20.
PW14/Lingaraju Police Sub-Inspector who received the information and visited the spot and obtained the complaint from PW1 and forwarded the same to police station for registering the FIR.
21. PW15/Srimathi who carried the cloth of the deceased and speaks about panchanama at Ex.P10.
PW16/ Eshwar, the police constable who carried the FIR to the court is an official witness.
T.G. Umesh, police constable who accompanied PSI to the spot i.e., PW14.
Kumar who is spot panch witness at Ex.P11 is an official witness and also turned hostile.

Eshwar who is cousin brother of deceased also speaks about attending the negotiation and cannot say whether amount was paid or not and also partly turned hostile and not supported the case of the prosecution regarding assault to the deceased by the accused.
25. PW20/Mutthuswamy, Dy.SP and the investigation officer who received further investigation from PW22 and filed the charge sheet.
26. PW21/Praveen KN., who is Tahzilar conducted inquest panchanama on the dead body and who recorded the statement of witness and sent the dead body to the post mortem examination.
PW22/Thirumalesh, head constable who registered the FIR by receiving the complaint and given to the PSI for investigation.
28. On perusal of the entire evidence of the prosecution except PW1 none of the witnesses speaks about he payment of dowry articles and cash to the accused.
PW6 and PW7 who is brother-in-law and sister of the deceased also turned hostile and have not supported the prosecution case.

The other witnesses are panch witness, the person who attended the marriage and negotiation of the marraige are all not fully supported the prosecution case, except stating that there was demand from the side of the accused for payment of dowry of Rs.70,000/- and 70 gms of gold and it was stated that they decided to give 50 gms of gold and Rs.40,000/- amount in cash but none of these witnesses stated whether this dowry articles and cash were given to the accused either prior to the marriage or after the marriage or on the date of the marriage.

Nagendra vs State Of Karnataka on 14 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189226210/
5 29.
The very sister of the deceased PW7 and her husband PW6 also not supported the prosecution case with respect of payment of dowry articles.

On perusal of entire evidence on record it reveals most of them speaks about negotiation of the marriage, demand of dowry articles but they have not stated payment of dowry articles or money paid to the accused.

Considering the same, the trial court rightly found, the accused not guilty for the offence punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of DP Act and also prosecution failed to prove that there was demand of dowry soon prior to the incident and due to the said incident, the deceased committed suicide.

31. Therefore, the trial court rightly acquitted the appellant/accused for the offence punishable under Section 304-B of IPC, except the ingredients that the death occurred within 7 years of marriage and there was some demand by the accused for purchasing the fertilizer for the crop, the PW1 said to have given Rs.7000/- long back is not correct as there was no demand of dowry and harassment soon prior to the deceased committing suicide.

32. Such being the case, the trial court though rightly found not guilty for the offence punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of DP act and section 304B of IPC but committed error in - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:20502 holding that the accused was found guilty for the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC.

For the purpose of bringing under the provisions of Section 304 B, there must be demand of dowry and harassment soon prior to the death of the deceased, but the same was not proved by the prosecution and none of the witness including the family members of the deceased,
sister and brother-in-law have not supported the case and mentioned that there was demand of dowry or harassment of the deceased soon prior to the incident of commission of the suicide.
33.
Such being the case, mere accused demanding some money for the purpose of purchasing fertilizer, that itself cannot be ground to show the accused harassed her physically and mentally.

As per section 498(A) of IPC, the explanation clearly defines that "(a) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand."
Here, in this case the trial court has held there was no demand of dowry after the marriage and harassment with the accused.
Such being the case, convicting the appellant under Section 498A, is not correct.

Therefore, the judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Nagendra vs State Of Karnataka on 14 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189226210/
6 court holding appellant guilty for the offence punishable under Section 498A deserves to be set aside.

Accordingly, I pass the following:-
This criminal appeal is allowed.
The judgment of conviction and sentence passed under Section 498(A) by the V Additional District and Sessions Judge, Mysuru in S.C.No.174/2010 is set aside.
